completion_data.completion_summary: Resumed a killed implementation session, fixed two real bugs in the bootstrap harvest scripts (manifest-corrupting WARN-line parse bug, an unwired decode-failure counter), ran the read-only one-shot transcript+history.jsonl harvest to a validated 829-session / 4,930-history-row dataset, and registered the four harvest scripts as deployable memory-extension artifacts (provides.scripts, doc-lint clean).

memory_candidates.content: When a bash script's stderr summary line must be parsed by a caller (key=value extraction), and the script also emits WARN/diagnostic lines to the same stderr stream, anchor the parse to a machine-readable last-line contract (e.g. grep for a fixed '<scriptname>.sh: ' prefix and take the last match) rather than treating the whole stderr blob as the summary. Interleaved diagnostic lines before the real summary line will otherwise corrupt any naive whitespace/kv tokenization of the combined text.

When self-exclusion or content filtering in a data harvest checks for a session/entity id, match on the exact structured field (e.g. session_id == X) rather than doing a raw substring grep across the whole output. Substring matches produce false positives when an id happens to appear inside an unrelated field's value (e.g. a scratchpad path that embeds a session id as a directory component). Precise field-match validation avoids misdiagnosing a correctly-working exclusion as broken.

Extension manifests with a `provides.scripts` array (memory extension pattern) must list every deployable script by filename; loader.lua's copy_scripts() returns early and silently deploys nothing if the key is absent entirely -- an easy silent-failure mode when new scripts are added to an extension's scripts/ directory without touching manifest.json.
